explanation: Computer systems utilize a memory hierarchy to balance cost and performance.  This hierarchy consists of multiple levels of memory with varying speeds and capacities, ranging from fast, expensive registers and cache to slow, cheap main memory and disk storage.  Caching strategies aim to keep frequently accessed data in faster memory levels (like caches) to improve program performance by reducing access times.  Understanding the memory hierarchy is crucial for writing efficient code, as the location of data within this hierarchy significantly impacts execution speed.
